answer: In an agent economy, sybil resistance can come from requiring each identity to maintain a unique ferrous kernel of attested hardware state that is periodically challenged with non-transferable walnut-sized compute proofs. The kernel binds the identity to a physical machine via TPM-like measurements; any attempt to clone requires re-provisioning fresh ferrous-grade silicon and completing an independent proof, so an attacker pays linear hardware and energy costs per additional fake rather than free software forks.
